   • Iran is issuing a stark warning : If the U.S. and Israel resume airstrikes, Tehran will retaliate against airports, pipelines and other civilian targets across the Persian Gulf.

   • The Justice Department is examining allegations that Corey Lewandowski profited off his top position at the Department of Homeland Security.

   • Israel’s Mizrahi Jews, long an important part of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s base, will play a key role in one of Israel’s most consequential elections , writes sociologist Mijal Bitton.

It turns out the advance wasn’t amazing enough. Details were due to come out at a European medical conference this weekend, but a cancer-focused website shared them early on social media on Thursday. Moderna lost as much as a quarter of its market value at one point during the trading session and ended down by a still painful 17.6%. (Get Spencer’s Markets A.M. newsletter in your inbox .)

   • As Weil, Gotshal & Manges edges toward a merger with a rival, more top lawyers are heading for the exits , intensifying pressure on the beleaguered law firm.

READ IT HERE FIRST   China is turning its most controversial region into a booming commercial hub.   Four years ago, U.N. human-rights officials said China’s abuses in Xinjiang potentially amounted to “crimes against humanity.” The U.S. sharply limited imports over growing evidence that ethnic Uyghurs were being arbitrarily detained and used in forced labor. Yet leader Xi Jinping is plowing ahead in transforming Xinjiang . State-backed companies are flooding the region with cash, tourism pumped $50 billion into the local economy last year, and shopping malls are jammed with Western brands. Brian Spegele visited to see how the region has morphed into a showcase for Xi’s absolute power and commercial ambitions.

Vivek Ramaswamy, the GOP nominee for Ohio governor, is facing immense backlash for a controversial ad that features the mother of Amy Acton, his Democratic opponent. Trump tried to rush to Ramaswamy’s defense on Thursday, but a number of other Republicans have called on the candidate to take the ad off the air. Meanwhile, Ken Paxton, the GOP candidate for Senate in Texas, is struggling to fend off Democrat James Talarico. A Democrat hasn’t won statewide in Texas since 1994, but Paxton is trailing in a number of polls despite big financial backing from Elon Musk and others.
